reading: The red (2) cells mark which side of the shape to reflect onto: the shape is mirrored across the line between itself and the red cells (red is overwritten), then the background becomes 3.

new_rows.name: shape
new_rows.datalog: shape(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), !px(Y, X, 2).

why: the non-red cells plus their reflection about the shape/red boundary give the output's foreground; every 0 becomes 3

reading: Every row or column whose interior (all cells except its two end cells) is entirely background gets its background cells painted 3.

new_rows.name: lane
new_rows.datalog:
maxx(max(X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
maxy(max(Y)) :- px(Y, X, C).
rowhit(Y) :- cell(Y, X, C), maxx(M), X > 0, X < M.
colhit(X) :- cell(Y, X, C), maxy(M), Y > 0, Y < M.
lane(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), !cell(Y, X, C), !rowhit(Y).
lane(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), !cell(Y, X, C), !colhit(X).

why: exactly the background cells of fully clear wall-to-wall rows/columns become 3

reading: A green path starts from the 2-cell green segment, runs along its direction, turns 90 degrees when the next cell is an 8 obstacle, and continues until it joins the 2-cell red segment.

slots.start: the 2-cell green (3) segment and its direction

why: the drawn 3 cells form one connected orthogonal path from green to red that never overlaps an 8

reading: Each row is inverted against its dominant colour: cells of the row's main colour become 0, and every other cell (0 or stray colours) becomes the main colour.

slots.key colour: the most common non-zero colour of that row
slots.map: main colour -> 0, everything else -> main colour

why: per row, the output is the complement of the main-colour cells, painted in the main colour

reading: Each 9-object carries a 6 stripe through its middle; the object is split into two halves at that middle, the 6 cells are erased, and the two halves each move one cell away from the split line.

slots.subject: each 9/6 object
slots.cut: the midline of the object perpendicular to the 6 stripe's long direction
slots.move: each half shifts 1 cell outward, away from the cut

why: every output 9 cell is an input 9 cell shifted by 1 away from its object's midline

reading: Each background cell diagonally up-left of a foreground cell (wrapping around the grid edges) becomes 2; the result is then tiled 3x3.

new_rows.name: diag
new_rows.datalog:
maxx(max(X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
maxy(max(Y)) :- px(Y, X, C).
bgc(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), !cell(Y, X, C).
diag(Y, X) :- bgc(Y, X), Y2 = Y + 1, X2 = X + 1, cell(Y2, X2, D).
diag(Y, X) :- bgc(Y, X), maxx(M), X = M, Y2 = Y + 1, X2 = 0, cell(Y2, X2, D).
diag(Y, X) :- bgc(Y, X), maxy(N), Y = N, Y2 = 0, X2 = X + 1, cell(Y2, X2, D).
diag(Y, X) :- bgc(Y, X), maxy(N), Y = N, maxx(M), X = M, Y2 = 0, X2 = 0, cell(Y2, X2, D).

why: output is 3H x 3W and every block equals the input with 2 added at the toroidal up-left diagonal of each fg cell

reading: Find the one colour that occurs exactly once; keep that cell, erase everything else, and surround it with a 3x3 ring of 2.
verb: isolate unique cell and frame it

new_rows.name: unique
new_rows.datalog:
ccount(C, count(Y, X)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
unique(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), ccount(C, N), N = 1.

why: the output has only the unique-colour cell plus the 8 cells around it in colour 2
invariants: position and colour of the unique cell

reading: All-background squares of side 2 or more are filled with 1, largest first and without overlap (greedy packing of zero squares).

slots.region: maximal all-0 k x k squares (k >= 2), chosen greedily from largest k down, scanning top-left to bottom-right, never overlapping already filled cells

why: filled cells are exactly the union of non-overlapping zero squares chosen greedily largest-first

reading: Each 1-object is classified: closed shapes (no gap from their hole to the outside, or solid) turn 2 and slide to the left edge; open shapes turn 3 and slide to the right edge, keeping their rows.

slots.subject: each 1-object
slots.test: whether its enclosed background is sealed (closed) or leaks to outside (open)
slots.closed: recolour 2, move horizontally to touch left border
slots.open: recolour 3, move horizontally to touch right border

why: every object keeps shape and row span; colour and side depend only on closure

reading: Inside the bounding box of the 8 cells, every 1 becomes 3; nothing else changes.

new_rows.name: inbox
new_rows.datalog:
eminy(min(Y)) :- px(Y, X, 8).
emaxy(max(Y)) :- px(Y, X, 8).
eminx(min(X)) :- px(Y, X, 8).
emaxx(max(X)) :- px(Y, X, 8).
inbox(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, 1), eminy(A), emaxy(B), eminx(C), emaxx(D), Y >= A, Y <= B, X >= C, X <= D.

why: exactly the 1 cells within the 8s' bounding box become 3
